subject: MAP: Weekly performance checkpoint — latency & throughput runbook
messages:

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: MAP weekly perf checkpoint — baseline and ask

Hi Alex / Acme team,

Quick status from our MAP performance thread ahead of next week's demo: we've completed the baseline runs against the customer prompt set and initial results are attached (benchmark_20260804_p95_latency.csv). Top-level notes: 
- p95 latency (hosted profile): 185ms for the 8k prompt set (avg seq len ~1.2k tokens)
- steady-state throughput: 210 req/s with 2x continuous batching
- tail variance: a few spikes up to ~420ms under isolated stress (short-lived)

Immediate asks:
1) Acme: confirm the representative prompt / traffic mix in the attached sample (Alex)
2) Redwood: we will propose a tuning runbook (batches, kv cache, quantization trade-offs) — will share by EOD next Tuesday

Attaching: benchmark_20260804_p95_latency.csv

Thanks,
Grace

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05T14:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: MAP weekly perf checkpoint — baseline and ask

Thanks Grace — quick follow-up from the infra side:
- Baseline runs used single model shard with int8 quantization; we saw the best p95 improvement when enabling prefix KV caching for repeated instructions (approx -30ms).
- Throughput ceiling at 210 req/s is consistent with the current autoscale cap; we can increase burst capacity for the demo but want to avoid swapping model variants during the call.

Proposed micro-actions:
- Rishi: enable persistent KV for the demo namespace and pre-warm caches (owner: rishi_malhotra) — ETA: 2026-08-10
- Marcus: run a focused throughput sweep (50–300 rps) with current batching config and log memory KPIs (owner: marcus_lin) — ETA: 2026-08-09

I'll collect the infra metrics and share a terse runbook draft by Monday.

Date: 2026-08-06T10:34:00-04:00
Subject: Re: MAP weekly perf checkpoint — runbook + evaluation plan

All — following up with the MAP/QA perspective. I sketched a short evaluation plan so the demo metrics tie back to Acme's success criteria:
- Success criteria (Acme): p95 < 200ms for 8k prompt set; sustained 200 req/s for 10 minutes without error spikes
- Eval plan: 3 run categories — baseline (no caching), tuned (KV + batching), and resilient (tuned + fallback to smaller variant)
- Measurement: record p50/p95/p99, memory pressure, model loaded latency, and error rate per run; identify regressions vs baseline using the regression harness

Action owners I recommend: 
- Run coordination & evaluation: Neha (neha_kapoor) — produce a short report (format: one-pager + CSV)
- Dashboard: Alex Martinez (alex_martinez) — wire up KPI dashboard tile for the Acme namespace (link will be shared)

I'll draft the evaluation checklist and attach the perf_runbook_v2.md for internal review.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Staff, Performance & Evaluation
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Alex Bradley <alex.bradley@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-08-10T11:58:00-04:00
Subject: Re: MAP weekly perf checkpoint — throughput sweep results

Sharing the focused throughput sweep results. Attached: benchmark_20260804_p95_latency.csv (trimmed) — key highlights: 
- 50 rps: p95 98ms, stable
- 150 rps: p95 132ms, stable
- 210 rps: p95 185ms, observed memory pressure on two workers, small GC events correlated to 310–420ms spikes
- 260 rps: p95 270ms, error rate ~0.4% under sustained 10m runs

Notes / recommendations: 
1) For the customer demo target (200 req/s sustained), the tuned profile (KV + increased batching to 3) hits p95 ~145ms in staging — good headroom.
2) We should enable autoscale burst to 2.5x for the demo window and pre-warm model caches 30min prior.
3) Marcus will upload CSV and a short memory KPI extract to the drive folder.

Attachments: benchmark_20260804_p95_latency.csv

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-11T16:05:00-04:00
Subject: MAP checkpoint — agreed runbook, owners, and demo timeline

Alex — thanks for the quick confirmation on the prompt set earlier this morning. Final recap and short next steps so it's actionable for procurement/demo: 
- Agreed customer success criteria: p95 < 200ms, sustain 200 req/s for 10m (no >1% errors)
- What Redwood will do before demo (owners & ETA):
  * Pre-warm KV & caches (owner: rishi_malhotra) — complete by 2026-08-11 22:00 EDT
  * Increase batching to 3 in the tuned profile and enable persistent KV (owner: rishi_malhotra) — config push 2026-08-11 20:00 EDT
  * Autoscale burst to 2.5x for the demo window (owner: marcus_lin) — scheduled for the demo hour
  * Run final 10m sustained test and upload report (owner: neha_kapoor) — ETA: 2026-08-11 23:30 EDT (report + CSV)
  * Dashboard tile for Acme namespace live (owner: alex_martinez) — ETA: 2026-08-11 18:00 EDT (link: see related_links)

Procurement / Alex: please confirm the demo time window (we propose 2026-08-12 15:00–16:00 EDT) so we can lock autoscale and reserve capacity.

Attachments: perf_runbook_v2.md, kpi_dashboard_link.txt

If there are no redlines, I'll mark this MAP checkpoint green and circulate the one-pager after the final run.

Best,
Grace
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
